title: no-cache still stores. Use no-store
question: no-store or private, no-cache?
fact_source: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9111#section-5.2.2.4 (no-cache: response MUST NOT be used to satisfy another request without validation; caches may store it) and #section-5.2.2.5 (no-store: a cache MUST NOT store any part of the request or response)

scenes.headline: no-cache, still on disk
scenes.voice: You sent no cache on the account page, but caches can still save a copy.
scenes.caption: You sent no-cache on the account page, but caches can still save a copy.

scenes.headline: no-cache = revalidate
scenes.voice: No cache does not mean do not store. It means caches may store it, but must revalidate before reuse.
scenes.caption: no-cache does not mean do not store. Caches may store it, but must revalidate before reuse.

scenes.headline: Send no-store
scenes.voice: For private data, send Cache-Control no store. Then caches must not store any part of it.
scenes.caption: For private data, send Cache-Control: no-store. Caches must not store any part of it.

scenes.headline: Stored copies: 1 → 0
scenes.voice: Now stored copies go from one to zero, straight from the HTTP caching spec.
scenes.caption: Now stored copies go from 1 to 0, straight from the HTTP caching spec.

scenes.voice: For a login page, which do you send: no store, or private with no cache? Comment your answer.
scenes.caption: For a login page, which do you send: no-store, or private with no-cache? Comment your answer.

scenes.caption: Follow K4Coding for part 8.
